name: Proper Unlabeled Sample Compression
definition: Let $\mathcal H\subseteq\{0,1\}^{X}$ be nonempty on a finite domain. A **proper unlabeled compression scheme of size $k$** consists of fixed maps $C$ and $\rho$: for every realizable partial labeled sample $s:S\to\{0,1\}$, the encoder selects an unordered key $C(s)\subseteq S$ with $|C(s)|\le k$, and $\rho(C(s))\in\mathcal H$ agrees with $s$ on $S$. The decoder receives only the coordinate key: no retained labels, original domain $S$, auxiliary messages, repetitions or ordering choices. The **Proper Unlabeled Sample Compression** $\mathrm{pUSC}(\mathcal H)$ is the least such $k$, or $+\infty$ if no scheme exists. No stability is imposed. Nonexistence can occur even for finite classes, for the balanced six-split class.
graph_summary: Fewest retained coordinates, without labels or messages, allowing reconstruction in the class; $+\infty$ if no proper unlabeled scheme exists.
origin_references: This is the proper-reconstruction restriction of the unlabeled-compression framework; see \cite{kuzmin2007unlabeled,palvolgyi2021unlabeled,chalopin2022unlabeled}.

p_monotonic.proof: On a sample of the projected class, apply the original proper scheme to that same sample on the retained coordinates and restrict its reconstruction.  An extension makes the sample realizable in $\mathcal H$; the restricted reconstruction is in the projected class and is consistent, without enlarging the unlabeled compression set.

comments: Conditioning monotonicity is unverified. The former append-compress-erase argument did not supply a well-defined decoder after distinct keys lose their fixed coordinates. An explicit collision disproves that construction for an ordinary proper encoder, not monotonicity of the parameter. The stable case requires a separate collision argument. See sync/COMPRESSION_CONDITIONING_AUDIT.md in the source repository (September 20, 2026).
